It was still a long way to them, so that it was not till noon of the third day from the rock-sea that they came to the very feet of that fire-scorched ness, and wonderful indeed it seemed to them that anything save the eagles could have aught to tell of what lay beyond it.

There were no foothills or downs betwixt the plain and the mountains, naught save a tumble of rocks that had fallen from the cliffs, piled up strangely, and making a maze through which the Sage led them surely; and at last they were clear even of this, and were underneath the flank of that ness, which was so huge that there seemed that there could scarce be any more mountain than that. Little of its huge height could they see, now they were close to it, for it went up sheer at first and then beetled over them till they could see no more of its side; as they wound about its flank, and they were long about it, the Sage cried out to those two and stretched out his hand, and behold! the side of the black cliff plain and smooth and shining as if it had been done by the hand of men or giants, and on this smooth space was carven in the living rock the image of a warrior in mail and helm of ancient fashion, and holding a sword in his right hand. From head to heel he seemed some sixty feet high, and the rock was so hard, that he was all clean and clear to see; and they deemed of him that his face was keen and stern of aspect.

===Chinese===

他们来到群山之门

那一天他们在附近放牧马匹，贤者不时考较二人，看他们是否把路上的学问记得纯熟；发觉他们一样不落，毫无遗漏。

当夜他们仍在原地歇下，次日一早起身，由贤者领着穿过平原赶路；走着走着，那群山和山中的恐怖仿佛就悬在他们头顶上，山的巍峨黢黑，比一道火墙还可怕。到山跟前还有好一段路，从离开岩石之海算起，直到第三天正午，他们才走到那道被地火烧灼过的山嘴脚下；在他们看来，除了鹰隼，居然还有生灵能知道山那边的事，这真不可思议。

平原与群山之间没有丘陵冈阜，只有从悬崖上崩落下来、堆积得奇形怪状的乱石，构成一座迷宫，贤者领着他们稳稳穿了过去；最后连乱石也走尽了，他们便到了那道山嘴的侧腹底下——山嘴如此巨大，仿佛天下再没有比它更多的山了。到了近处，它巍峨的高度反倒看不见多少，因为先是笔直上去，继而倾覆过来压在他们头顶，侧面再什么也瞧不见；他们沿着它的侧腹绕行，绕了很久，忽然贤者向二人喊了一声，伸手一指，看哪！黑色的崖壁上有一片平整光滑、莹然发亮的地方，象是出于人或巨人之手；就在这平滑的石面上，就着山岩本色刻着一尊武士像，披古式的锁子甲、戴古式的头盔，右手握着一柄剑。从头顶到脚跟，他约有六十尺高；岩石坚硬，所以像身干净清晰，历历可见。他们觉得他那副面容，精悍而威严。

===Original===

So there they stood in an awful bight of the mountain, made by that ness, and the main wall from which it thrust out. But after they had gazed awhile and their hearts were in their mouths, the Sage turned on those twain and said: “Here then is the end of my journey with you; and ye wot all that I can tell you, and I can say no word more save to bid you cast all fear aside and thrive. Ye have yet for this day’s journey certain hours of such daylight as the mountain pass will give you, which at the best is little better than twilight; therefore redeem ye the time.”

But Ralph got off his horse, and Ursula did in likewise, and they both kissed and embraced the old man, for their hearts were full and fain. But he drew himself away from them, and turned about with no word more, and went his ways, and presently was hidden from their eyes by the rocky maze which lay about the mountain’s foot. Then the twain mounted their horses again and set forth silently on the road, as they had been bidden.

In a little while the rocks of the pass closed about them, leaving but a way so narrow that they could see a glimmer of the stars above them as they rode the twilight; no sight they had of the measureless stony desert, yet in their hearts they saw it. They seemed to be wending a straight-walled prison without an end, so that they were glad when the dark night came on them.

===Chinese===

于是他们站在山的一处骇人的湾澳里——那是由山嘴和它所伸出的主山墙夹成的。他们凝望了一阵，心都提到了嗓子眼；随后贤者转过身来，对两人说：「我与你们同行，到这里就到头了；我能告诉你们的，你们都知道了，再没有别的话可说，只有一句：抛开一切恐惧，好生兴旺。今日这段路，山隘里还能给你们几个钟头的亮光，那亮光至多也不过同暮色差不多；所以要抓紧时辰。」

拉尔夫下了马，厄休拉也随着下来，两人都亲吻拥抱老人，因为心里满是眷恋。他却从他们怀抱中挣脱出来，一言不发地转过身，自去了；不多时，山脚周围的乱石迷宫便把他的身影遮没，再也看不见了。于是两人重新上马，依照嘱咐，默默地踏上路程。

不多时，隘口的岩石把他们夹在中间，只剩一条窄路，走在暮色里，抬头只见头顶上一线星光；那无边无际的石头荒漠他们望不见了，心里却看得见。他们象是在一座四壁陡立的、没有尽头的监狱里赶路，因此黑夜到来时，他们反倒高兴。

===Original===

Ralph found some shelter in the cleft of a rock above a mound where was little grass for the horses. He drew Ursula into it, and they sat down there on the stones together. So long they sat silent that a great gloom settled upon Ralph, and he scarce knew whether he were asleep or waking, alive or dead. But amidst of it fell a sweet voice on his ears, and familiar words asking him of what like were the fields of Upmeads, and the flowers; and of the fish of its water, and of the fashion of the building of his father’s house; and of his brethren, and the mother that bore him. Then was it to him at first as if a sweet dream had come across the void of his gloom, and then at last the gloom and the dread and the deadness left him, and he knew that his friend and fellow was talking to him, and that he sat by her knee to knee, and the sweetness of her savoured in his nostrils as she leaned her face toward him, and he knew himself for what he was; and yet for memory of that past horror, and the sweetness of his friend and whatnot else, he fell a-weeping. But Ursula bestirred herself and brought out food from her wallet, and sat down beside him again, and he wiped the tears from his eyes and laughed, and chid himself for being as a child in the dark, and then they ate and drank together in that dusk nook of the wilderness. And now was he happy and his tongue was loosed, and he fell to telling her many things of Upmeads, and of the tale of his forefathers, and of his old loves and his friends, till life and death seemed to him as they had seemed of time past in the merry land of his birth. So there anon they fell asleep for weariness, and no dreams of terror beset their slumbers.

===Chinese===

拉尔夫在一处土冈上找到一个岩缝可以栖身，冈上有一点草，好歹够马吃。他把厄休拉拉进岩缝，两人便一起坐在石头上。他们默默坐了许久，一片巨大的阴郁压上了拉尔夫的心头，他几乎分不清自己是睡着还是醒着，是活着还是死了。正在这时，一个甜美的声音落进他耳中，说的是些熟悉的话，问他阿普米兹的田野是什么模样、有什么花；问那水里的鱼，问他父亲房屋的建制格局；问他的兄弟，问生养他的母亲。起初他觉得，象是一场甜梦飘过他阴郁的虚空；到后来，阴郁、恐惧和麻木全都离他而去，他知道是他的朋友、他的旅伴在对他说话，知道他与她膝挨着膝坐在一处，她把脸凑近他时，发肤的芬芳沁入他的鼻息；他认清了自己究竟是谁。然而，想起方才那阵恐怖，又感受着朋友的温存和种种情味，他哭了起来。厄休拉赶忙起身，从行囊里取出食物，又坐到他身旁；他抹去眼泪，笑了一笑，怪自己象个怕黑的孩子；随后两人便在那荒野的幽暗角落里一同吃喝。这时他快活起来，话匣子也打开了，便对她说起阿普米兹的种种，说起祖辈的故事，说起旧日的情人和朋友，直到生与死在他心里又恢复了旧时光故乡乐土上的分量。不久，两人便因疲惫沉沉睡去，梦中再无恐怖相扰。

## XI / 十一
===Original===

They Come to the Vale of Sweet Chestnuts

When they went on their way next morning they found little change in the pass, and they rode the dread highway daylong, and it was still the same: so they rested a little before nightfall at a place where there was water running out of the rocks, but naught else for their avail. Ralph was merry and helpful and filled water from the runnel, and wrought what he might to make the lodging meet; and as they ate and rested he said to Ursula: “Last night it was thou that beguiled me of my gloom, yet thereafter till we slept it was my voice for the more part, and not thine, that was heard in the wilderness. Now tonight it shall be otherwise, and I will but ask a question of thee, and hearken to the sweetness of thy voice.”

She laughed a little and very sweetly, and she said: “Forsooth, dear friend, I spoke to thee that I might hear thy voice for the more part, and not mine, that was heard in the desert; but when I heard thee, I deemed that the world was yet alive for us to come back to.”

He was silent awhile, for his heart was pierced with the sweetness of her speech, and he had fain have spoken back as sweetly as a man might; yet he could not because he feared her somewhat, lest she should turn cold to him; therefore himseemed that he spoke roughly, as he said: “Nevertheless, my friend, I beseech thee to tell me of thine old home, even as last night I told thee of mine.”

“Yea,” she said, “with a good will.” And straightway she fell to telling him of her ways when she was little, and of her father and mother, and of her sister that had died, and the brother whom Ralph had seen at Bourton Abbas: she told also of bachelors who had wooed her, and jested concerning them, yet kindly and without malice, and talked so sweetly and plainly, that the wilderness was become a familiar place to Ralph, and he took her hand in the dusk and said: “But, my friend, how was it with the man for whom thou wert weeping when I first fell in with thee at Bourton Abbas?”

===Chinese===

他们来到甜栗之谷

次日早晨上路，隘口没什么变化，他们在这条骇人的大道上走了一整天，仍是老样子；黄昏前他们在一处从岩缝里出水的地方稍事歇息，此外再没有什么可用的东西。拉尔夫兴冲冲地张罗，从小溪里打满了水，尽力把宿处收拾妥帖；吃喝休息时，他对厄休拉说：「昨夜是你把我从阴郁里哄了出来，可从那时直到入睡，荒野里听见的多半是我的声音，不是你的。今夜要换个样儿：我只问你一个问题，然后就来听你那甜美的嗓音。」

她轻轻一笑，笑得极甜，说：「说实在的，亲爱的朋友，我对你说话，正是为了荒野里响起的多半是你的声音，而不是我的；我听你说话时，便觉得这世界还活着，等我们回去。」

他沉默了一会儿，因为她话语的甜美刺进了他的心；他很想也用一个男人所能有的甜言回敬她，却做不到，因为他有点怕她，怕她对他冷下来；于是说出来的话显得粗声粗气：「不过，我的朋友，求你给我讲讲你从前的家吧，就象昨夜我给你讲我的家那样。」

「好啊，」她说，「我乐意讲。」于是她立刻讲起小时候的种种，讲她的父亲母亲，讲她那个死去的姐姐，还有拉尔夫在伯顿阿巴斯见过的那个兄弟；她也讲到那些向她求过亲的单身汉，拿他们打趣，却怀着善意、不带刻薄。她说得又甜美又坦白，荒野在拉尔夫听来竟成了亲切的地方；他在暮色里握住她的手说：「可是，我的朋友，我在伯顿阿巴斯头一回遇见你时，你为他哭的那个人，又是怎么一回事？」

===Original===

She said: “I will tell thee plainly, as a friend may to a friend. Three hours had not worn from thy departure ere tidings came to me concerning him, that neither death nor wounding had befallen him; and that his masterless horse and bloodstained saddle were but a device to throw dust into our eyes, so that there might be no chase after him by the men of the Abbot’s bailiff, and that he might lightly do as he would, to wit, swear himself into the riders of the Burg of the Four Friths; for, in sooth, he was weary of me and mine. Yet further, I must needs tell thee that I know now, that when I wept before thee it was partly in despite, because I had found out in my heart (though I bade it not tell me so much) that I loved him but little.”

“Yea,” said Ralph, “and when didst thou come to that knowledge of thine heart?”

“Dear friend,” she said, “mayhappen I may tell thee hereafter, but as now I will forbear.” He laughed for joy of her, and in a little that talk fell down between them.

Despite the terror of the desert and the lonely ways, when Ralph laid him down on his stony bed, happiness wrapped his heart about. Albeit all this while he durst not kiss or caress her, save very measurely, for he deemed that she would not suffer it; nor as yet would he ask her wherefore, though he had it in his mind that he would not always forbear to ask her.

Many days they rode that pass of the mountains, though it was not always so evil and dreadful as at the first beginning; for now again the pass opened out into little valleys, wherein was foison of grass and sweet waters withal, and a few trees. In such places must they needs rest them, to refresh their horses as well as themselves, and to gather food, of venison, and wild-fruit and nuts. But abiding in such vales was very pleasant to them.

At last these said valleys came often and oftener, till it was so that all was pretty much one valley, whiles broken by a mountain neck, whiles straitened by a ness of the mountains that jutted into it, but never quite blind: yet was the said valley very high up, and as it were a trench of the great mountain. So they were glad that they had escaped from that strait prison betwixt the rock-walls, and were well at ease: and they failed never to find the tokens that led them on the way, even as they had learned of the Sage, so that they were not beguiled into any straying.

===Chinese===

她说：「我坦白告诉你吧，朋友对朋友本该如此。你走了还不到三个钟头，关于他的消息就传到了我耳朵里：他既没死也没受伤；那匹无主的马和染血的鞍子不过是遮人耳目的把戏，好让修道院总管的手下不去追赶他，好让他从容行事——也就是说，宣誓投到四弗里斯堡的骑士队里去；因为说实在的，他早厌烦了我和我家里的人。还有一层，我必须告诉你：如今我知道了，当初在你面前哭，一半是气不过，因为我心里已经明白（虽然我不许它告诉我这么多）：我实在不怎么爱他。」

「哦，」拉尔夫说，「那你是什么时候知道你这颗心的呢？」

「亲爱的朋友，」她说，「往后我也许会告诉你，眼下就先不说吧。」他因她这话而欢喜地笑了；不多时，这场谈话便自然止住了。

尽管荒野可怖、道路孤寂，拉尔夫躺上他那石头床时，幸福还是把他的心包裹起来。只是这一路他都不敢吻她、爱抚她，至多极有分寸地碰一碰，因为他觉得她不会容许；他也还不问她缘由，尽管心里已拿定主意，不会永远不问。

他们在这条山隘里走了许多天，虽然并不总象起初那样险恶可怕；因为隘口又渐渐敞开成一个个小山谷，谷中水草丰美、清泉甘洌，还有几棵树。在这样的地方，他们必定要歇息，让人和马都恢复气力，还要采集食物——野味、野果和坚果。而在这样的山谷里流连，实在是很惬意的事。

后来这样的山谷出现得越来越频繁，到后来几乎连成了一条谷：时而被一段山颈隔断，时而被一道伸进谷中的山嘴收窄，却从不曾完全堵死。只是这条谷地势很高，就象大山身上的一道沟槽。他们庆幸自己逃出了那座石壁夹成的窄狱，如今安稳自在；他们也从不曾找不到引路的标记——全按贤者所教的认去——因此不曾误入歧途。

===Original===

And now they had worn away thirty days since they had parted from the Sage, and the days began to shorten and the nights to lengthen apace; when on the forenoon of a day, after they had ridden a very rugged mountain-neck, they came down and down into a much wider valley into which a great reef of rocks thrust out from the high mountain, so that the northern half of the said vale was nigh cleft atwain by it; well grassed was the vale, and a fair river ran through it, and there were on either side the water great groves of tall and great sweet-chestnuts and walnut trees, whereon the nuts were now ripe. They rejoiced as they rode into it; for they remembered how the Sage had told them thereof, that their travel and toil should be stayed there awhile, and that there they should winter, because of the bread which they could make them of the chestnuts, and the plenty of walnuts, and that withal there was foison of venison.

So they found a ford of the river and crossed it, and went straight to the head of the rocky ness, being shown thither by the lore of the Sage, and they found in the face of the rock the mouth of a cavern, and beside it the token of the sword and the branch. Therefore they knew that they had come to their winter house, and they rejoiced thereat, and without more ado they got off their horses and went into the cavern. The entry thereof was low, so that they must needs creep into it, but within it was a rock-hall, high, clean and sweet-smelling.

There then they dight their dwelling, doing all they might to be done with their work before the winter was upon them. The day after they had come there they fell to on the ingathering of their chestnut harvest, and they dried them, and made them into meal; and the walnuts they gathered also. Withal they hunted the deer, both great and small; amongst which Ralph, not without some peril, slew two great bears, of which beasts, indeed, there was somewhat more than enough, as they came into the dale to feed upon the nuts and the berry-trees. So they soon had good store of peltries for their beds and their winter raiment, which Ursula fell to work on deftly, for she knew all the craft of needlework; and, shortly to tell it, they had enough and to spare of victual and raiment.

===Chinese===

到这时，他们离开贤者已经过了三十天，白昼渐短，黑夜迅速变长；一天上午，他们骑过一段极为崎岖的山颈，一路往下走，走进一条宽阔得多的山谷；一道巨大的礁石脉从高山伸进谷中，几乎把谷的北半边劈成两半。谷中水草丰茂，一条美丽的河穿谷而过，河两岸有大片高大茂美的甜栗树和核桃树林，果子这时都熟了。骑进谷中时，他们满心欢喜；因为他们记得贤者讲过这地方：他们的跋涉劳苦将在这里停歇一段时日，要在这里过冬——栗子可以做面包，核桃有的是，野味也丰足。

于是他们找到一处浅滩涉水过河，循着贤者所授的学问，径直走向那道石嘴的尽头，在岩壁上找到一个洞口，旁边刻着剑与树枝的记号。于是他们知道已经到了过冬的居所，心中欢喜，二话不说便下马进洞。洞口低矮，只能爬着进去；里面却是一座石厅，高敞、洁净，气息清新。

于是他们布置起住处，赶在冬天到来之前把活计都做完。到那里的第二天，他们便动手收栗子，把栗子晒干、磨成粉；核桃也采了不少。他们也猎捕大小鹿类；拉尔夫还冒着几分险，宰了两头大熊——这种野兽来谷中吃坚果和浆果树，实在多得过了头。于是他们很快攒下不少兽皮，用来铺床、做冬衣；厄休拉操起针线活来十分灵巧，因为她精通女红。长话短说：吃穿用度，他们都绰绰有余了。

## XII / 群山中的冬天
===Original===

Winter Amidst of the Mountains

In all this they had enough to be busy with, so that time hung not heavy on their hands, and the shadow of the Quest was nowise burdensome to them, since they wotted that they had to abide the wearing of the days till spring was come with fresh tidings. Their labour was nowise irksome to them, since Ralph was deft in all manner of sports and crafts, such as upcountry folk follow, and though he were a king’s son, he had made a doughty yeoman: and as for Ursula, she also was country-bred, of a lineage of field-folk, and knew all the manners of the fields.

Withal in whatsoever way it were, they loved each other dearly, and all kind of speech flowed freely betwixt them. Sooth to say, Ralph, taking heed of Ursula, deemed that she were fain to love him bodily, and he wotted well by now, that, whatever had befallen, he loved her, body and soul. Yet still was that fear of her naysay lurking in his heart, if he should kiss her, or caress her, as a man with a maid. Therefore he forbore, though desire of her tormented him grievously at whiles.

They wore their armour but little now, save when they were about some journey wherein was peril of wild beasts. Ursula had dight her some due woman’s raiment betwixt her knight’s surcoat and doeskins which they had gotten, so that it was not unseemly of fashion. As for their horses, they but seldom backed them, but used them to draw stuff to their rock-house on sledges, which they made of tree-boughs; so that the beasts grew fat, feeding on the grass of the valley and the wild-oats withal, which grew at the upper end of the bight of the valley, toward the northern mountains, where the ground was sandy. No man they saw, nor any signs of man, nor had they seen any save the Sage, since those riders of Utterbol had vanished before them into the night.

So wore autumn into winter, and the frost came, and the snow, with prodigious winds from out of the mountains: yet was not the weather so hard but that they might go forth most days, and come to no hurt if they were wary of the drifts; and forsooth needs must they go abroad to take venison for their livelihood.

So the winter wore also amidst sweet speech and friendliness betwixt the two, and they lived still as dear friends, and not as lovers.

===Chinese===

所有这些活计够他们忙碌的，日子并不难捱，求索之旅的阴影也丝毫不觉沉重，因为他们知道，必须安心消磨这些时日，等春天带来新的消息。劳作一点也不使他们烦苦：拉尔夫精于乡野之人擅长的各式技艺和活计，他虽是王子，却已锻炼成一个能干的庄户人；至于厄休拉，她也是乡下长大的，出身田家世系，田间的一套样样在行。

再说，无论怎么讲，他们都深深地相爱着，彼此无话不谈。说实话，拉尔夫留心观察厄休拉，觉得她未尝不愿以身相许；而他如今也十分明白，不管发生过什么，他都爱她——灵魂和肉体都爱。可倘若他像男人对少女那样去吻她、爱抚她，仍怕遭到她的拒绝——这份恐惧始终潜伏在他心里。因此他克制着，尽管对她的渴望时常苦苦煎熬着他。

如今他们很少穿戴甲胄了，除非出门赶路、有野兽之险的时候。厄休拉用她的骑士罩袍和弄来的鹿皮，给自己缝制了几件像样的女人衣裳，式样并不寒碜。至于马匹，他们也很少骑，只是让它们拉着雪橇往岩屋运东西——雪橇是用树枝做的；牲口吃着谷中的青草，还有谷湾上端朝北山那边沙地上长的野燕麦，一个个养得膘肥体壮。他们没有见到任何人，也没有人的踪迹；自从乌特博尔的骑手在他们眼前消失在黑夜里之后，他们除贤者外再没见过任何人。

就这样，秋去冬来，霜降雪落，山中刮起狂暴的大风：不过天气还不算太严酷，大多数日子他们仍能出门，只要提防雪堆就伤不着；而且为了猎取野味糊口，他们也非出门不可。

冬天就在两人的甜言蜜语与温存情谊中过去，他们依旧以挚友相待，而非恋人。

===Original===

Seldom they spoke of the Quest, for it seemed to them now a matter over great for speech. But now they were grown so familiar each to each that Ursula took heart to tell Ralph more of the tidings of Utterbol, for now the shame and grief of her bondage there was but as a story told of another, so far away seemed that time from this. But so grievous was her tale that Ralph grew grim thereover, and he said: “By St. Nicholas! it were a good deed, once we are past the mountains again, to ride to Utterbol and drag that swine and wittol from his hall and slay him, and give his folk a good day. But then there is thou, my friend, and how shall I draw thee into deadly strife?”

“Nay,” she said, “whereso thou ridest thither will I, and one fate shall lie on us both. We will think thereof and ask the Sage of it when we return. Who knows what shall have befallen then? Remember the lighting of the candle of Utterbol that we saw from the Rock-sea, and the boding thereof.” So Ralph was appeased for that time.

Oft also they spake of the little lands whence they came, and on a time amidst of such talk Ursula said: “But alas, friend, why do I speak of all this, when now save for my brother, who loveth me but after a fashion, to wit that I must in all wise do his bidding, lad as he is, I have no longer kith nor kin there, save again as all the folk of one stead are somewhat akin. I think, my dear, that I have no country, nor any house to welcome me.”

Said Ralph: “All lands, any land that thou mayst come to, shall welcome thee, and I shall look to it that so it shall be.” And in his heart he thought of the welcome of Upmeads, and of Ursula sitting on the dais of the hall of the High-House.

===Chinese===

他们很少谈起那求索之旅，因为如今在他们看来，那是件大得难以言说的事。但两人已亲密无间，厄休拉便鼓起勇气，把乌特博尔的种种遭遇讲给拉尔夫听——如今她在那里为奴的耻辱与悲苦，已恍如别人的故事，那段时光离眼下实在太远了。可她的故事太惨痛，拉尔夫听得面色铁青，说道："圣尼古拉斯在上！等我们再翻过群山，真该骑马杀到乌特博尔，把那头猪猡、那个甘戴绿帽的废物从他的厅堂里拖出来宰了，让他手下的家伙们也痛快痛快。可是还有你呢，我的朋友，我怎能把你拖进殊死的血战里去？"

"不，"她说，"你骑到哪儿，我就跟到哪儿，咱们俩同担一个命运。这件事咱们回去再从长计议，问问贤者的意思。谁知道到那时又会发生什么呢？还记得咱们在石海上望见乌特博尔那边烛火燃起，还有那凶兆吧。"拉尔夫这才平了气。

他们也常谈起各自故乡的小小家园。一次闲谈间，厄休拉说："唉，朋友，我干吗还说这些呢——如今那边除了我哥哥，我已没有别的亲人了；而他爱我也要打折扣，就是说，他虽不过是个少年，我却得事事听他的。虽说同一个村子里的人多少都沾亲带故，可那算不得数。亲爱的，我想，我已经没有故土，也没有一户欢迎我归去的家门了。"

拉尔夫说："所有的国土，任何你将去的地方，都会欢迎你，这一点我会办到。"他心里想着阿普米兹的欢迎仪式，想着厄休拉坐在高宅大厅上首的情景。

===Original===

So wore the days till Candlemass, when the frost broke and the snows began to melt, and the waters came down from the mountains, so that the river rose over its banks and its waters covered the plain parts of the valley, and those two could go dry-shod but a little way out of their cavern; no further than the green mound or toft which lay at the mouth thereof: but the waters were thronged with fowl, as mallard and teal and coots, and of these they took what they would. Whiles also they waded the shallows of the flood, and whiles poled a raft about it, and so had pleasure of the waters as before they had had of the snow. But when at last the very spring was come, and the grass began to grow after the showers had washed the plain of the waterborne mud, and the snowdrop had thrust up and blossomed, and the celandine had come, and then when the blackthorn bloomed and the Lent-lilies hid the grass betwixt the great chestnut-boles, when the sun shone betwixt the showers and the west wind blew, and the throstles and blackbirds ceased not their song betwixt dawn and dusk, then began Ralph to say to himself, that even if the Well at the World’s End were not, and all that the Sage had told them was but a tale of Swevenham, yet were all better than well if Ursula were but to him a woman beloved rather than a friend. And whiles he was pensive and silent, even when she was by him, and she noted it and forbore somewhat the sweetness of her glances, and the caressing of her soft speech: though oft when he looked on her fondly, the blood would rise to her cheeks, and her bosom would heave with the thought of his desire, which quickened hers so sorely, that it became a pain and grief to her.

===Chinese===

日子就这样一天天过去，到了圣烛节，霜冻消解，积雪开始融化，山水滚滚而下，河水漫过堤岸，淹没了谷中的平地；两人出了洞穴，能不湿鞋走到的范围不过一小段——最远只到洞口那座绿丘土墩；水面上却挤满了水禽：绿头鸭、水鸭、白骨顶，要多少有多少。他们时而蹚着浅水，时而撑着木筏在水上荡来荡去，从这大水里得到了乐趣，正像先前从雪里得到的一样。

等到真正的春天来临，骤雨洗净了平原上洪水淤下的泥浆，青草开始生长，雪花莲钻出地面开花了，白屈菜也来了，接着黑刺李开花，四旬百合把大栗树干之间的草地遮得满满当当；阵雨间隙阳光照耀，西风吹拂，画眉和乌鸫从黎明到黄昏歌声不断——这时拉尔夫开始暗自思量：就算世界尽头之泉并不存在，贤者讲给他们的一切不过是斯韦文汉的一个故事，只要厄休拉做他的爱人而不只是朋友，那也比什么都好。

他时而沉思默想，缄口不言，即使她在身旁也这样；她察觉了，便稍稍收敛了眼波的甜蜜和软语的温存：然而每当他的目光深情地落在她身上，她的脸就会泛起红晕，胸脯因想到他的渴望而起伏——那渴望也深深激起了她的，激得那样强烈，竟成了她的痛苦和忧伤。

## XIII / 十三
===Original===

Of Ursula and the Bear

It befell on a fair sunny morning of spring, that Ralph sat alone on the toft by the rock-house, for Ursula had gone down the meadow to disport her and to bathe in the river. Ralph was fitting the blade of a dagger to a long ashen shaft, to make him a strong spear; for with the waxing spring the bears were often in the meadows again; and the day before they had come across a family of the beasts in the sandy bight under the mountains; to wit a carle, and a quean with her cubs; the beasts had seen them but afar off, and whereas the men were two and the sun shone back from their weapons, they had forborne them; although they were fierce and proud in those wastes, and could not away with creatures that were not of their kind. So because of this Ralph had bidden Ursula not to fare abroad without her sword, which was sharp and strong, and she no weakling withal. He bethought him of this just as he had made an end of his spear-shaping, so therewith he looked aside and saw the said sword hanging to a bough of a little quicken-tree, which grew hard by the door. Fear came into his heart therewith, so he arose and strode down over the meadow hastily bearing his new spear, and girt with his sword. Now there was a grove of chestnuts betwixt him and the river, but on the other side of them naught but the green grass down to the water’s edge.

===Chinese===

厄休拉与熊

那是春天一个晴朗的早晨，拉尔夫独自坐在石屋旁的土墩上，厄休拉下草场玩耍、到河里洗澡去了。拉尔夫正把一柄匕首的刃装上长长的白蜡木杆，给自己做一支结实的长矛；因为随着春天渐深，熊又时常到草场上来了；前一天，他们还在山脚下的沙湾里撞见一家子熊——公熊一只，母熊带着几只崽子。那些野兽只是远远望见他们，又因对方是两个人、兵器上反射着阳光，才没有过来为难；虽说它们在这片荒野里凶猛高傲，容不得异类。正因为这个，拉尔夫吩咐过厄休拉：出门不可不带剑。那剑锋利结实，她也不是弱女子。矛刚做好，他想起了这事，便朝旁边一望，看见那把剑正挂在门边一株小花楸树的枝桠上。恐惧顿时涌上心头，他霍地起身，提着新矛、佩着剑，匆匆穿过草场大步赶去。他和河之间有一片栗树林，林子那一边，直到水边，只有青青的草地。

===Original===

Sure enough as he came under the trees he heard a shrill cry, and knew that it could be naught save Ursula; so he ran thitherward whence came the cry, shouting as he ran, and was scarce come out of the trees ere he saw Ursula indeed, mother-naked, held in chase by a huge bear as big as a bullock: he shouted again and ran the faster; but even therewith, whether she heard and saw him, and hoped for timely help, or whether she felt her legs failing her, she turned on the bear, and Ralph saw that she had a little axe in her hand wherewith she smote hardily at the beast; but he, after the fashion of his kind, having risen to his hind legs, fenced with his great paws like a boxer, and smote the axe out of her hand, and she cried out bitterly and swerved from him and fell a running again; but the bear tarried not, and would have caught her in a few turns; but even therewith was Ralph come up, who thrust the beast into the side with his long-headed spear, and not waiting to pull it out again, drew sword in a twinkling, and smote a forepaw off him and then drave the sword in over the shoulder so happily that it reached his heart, and he fell over dead with a mighty thump.

Then Ralph looked around for Ursula; but she had already run back to the riverside and was casting her raiment on her; so he awaited her beside the slain bear, but with drawn sword, lest the other bear should come upon them; for this was the he-bear. Howbeit he saw naught save presently Ursula all clad and coming towards him speedily; so he turned toward her, and when they met he cast himself upon her without a word, and kissed her greedily; and she forbore not at all, but kissed and caressed him as if she could never be satisfied.

So at last they drew apart a little, and walked quietly toward the rock-house hand in hand. And on the way she told him that even as she came up on to the bank from the water she saw the bear coming down on her as fast as he could drive, and so she but caught up her axe, and ran for it: “Yet I had little hope, dear friend,” she said, “but that thou shouldst be left alone in the wilderness.” And therewith she turned on him and cast her arms about him again, all weeping for joy of their two lives.

===Chinese===

果然，他刚走到树下，就听见一声尖利的喊叫，知道那必是厄休拉；便朝喊声传来的一边奔去，一面跑一面喊；刚出树林，便看见厄休拉果然在那里——浑身赤裸，正被一头公牛般大的巨熊追着。他又喊了一声，跑得更快；恰在此时，不知她是听见望见了他、指望救援及时，还是觉得两腿发软，她竟转身面对那熊；拉尔夫看见她手里握着一把小斧，勇敢地朝那野兽劈去；那熊照它们一族的路数，人立起来，象拳师一样挥动大掌招架，一掌把斧子打飞；她惨叫一声，闪身又要跑；熊却不放松，几个起落就要追上她；恰在这时拉尔夫赶到了，一矛捅进熊的胁下，也不等拔出，眨眼间抽出剑，剁下它一只前掌，随即从肩上直刺进去，正中心脏——那熊轰然一声倒地死了。

拉尔夫四下里找厄休拉；她已经跑回河边，正在穿衣；他便守在死熊旁边等她，剑仍出着鞘，防备另一头熊——这是头公熊——扑来。却没有见着什么，不多时只见厄休拉穿戴整齐，快步向他走来；他转身向她，两人一相遇，他一言不发便扑上去，热烈地吻她；她也毫不推拒，回吻他、爱抚他，仿佛永远不能满足似的。

后来两人稍稍分开，手拉着手，静静地朝石屋走去。路上她告诉他，她刚从水里上岸，就看见那熊全速朝她扑来，她只来得及抓起斧子就跑：「亲爱的朋友，我原本几乎不抱指望，」她说，「只想着你怕要独自一人留在荒野里了。」说着她转过身来，又伸出双臂搂住他，为两条性命欢喜得直落泪。

===Original===

Thus slowly they came before the door of their rock-house and Ralph said: “Let us sit down here on the grass, and if thou art not over wearied with the flight and the battle, I will ask thee a question.” She laid herself down on the grass with a sigh, yet it was as of one who sighs for pleasure and rest, and said, as he sat down beside her: “I am fain to rest my limbs and my body, but my heart is at rest; so ask on, dear friend.”

The song of birds was all around them, and the scent of many blossoms went past on the wings of the west wind, and Ralph was silent a little as he looked at the loveliness of his friend; then he said: “This is the question; of what kind are thy kisses this morning, are they the kisses of a friend or a lover? Wilt thou not called me beloved and not friend? Shall not we two lie on the bridal bed this same night?”

She looked on him steadily, smiling, but for love and sweetness, not for shame and folly; then she said: “O, dear friend and dearest lover, three questions are these and not one; but I will answer all three as my heart biddeth me. And first, I will tell thee that my kisses are as thine; and if thine are aught but the kisses of love, then am I befooled. And next, I say that if thou wilt be my friend indeed, I will not spare to call thee beloved, or to be all thy friend. But as to thy third question; tell me, is there not time enough for that?”

She faltered as she spake, but he said: “Look, beloved, and see how fair the earth is today! What place and what season can be goodlier than this? And were it not well that we who love each other should have our full joy out of this sweet season, which as now is somewhat marred by our desire?”

“Ah, beloved!” she said, looking shyly at him, “is it so marred by that which marreth not us?”

“Hearken!” he said; “how much longer shall this fairness and peace, and our leisure and safety endure? Here and now the earth rejoiceth about us, and there is none to say us nay; but tomorrow it may all be otherwise. Bethink thee, dear, if but an hour ago the monster had slain thee, and rent thee ere we had lain in each other’s arms!”

===Chinese===

他们慢慢走到石屋门前，拉尔夫说：「我们就在这草地上坐坐吧；要是追逐和搏斗没把你累坏，我有话问你。」她叹了口气，在草地上躺下来——却是那种舒坦憩息的叹息；他在她身旁坐下时，她说：「我的四肢和身子想歇歇，心却是安安稳稳的；问吧，亲爱的朋友。」

四周鸟声盈耳，百花的香气乘着西风之翼掠过。拉尔夫望着朋友的美丽，沉默了片刻，然后说：「问题是这样的：今早你那些吻，是哪一种吻？是朋友的吻，还是爱人的吻？你可肯让我叫你爱人而不叫朋友？我们两人今夜可要同入洞房？」

她定定地望着他，微笑着——那微笑是爱与甜蜜，不是羞惭和痴态；然后她说：「啊，亲爱的朋友、最亲爱的爱人，这是三个问题，不止一个；可我心口如一，三个都答。第一，我告诉你：我的吻就同你的吻一样；你的吻若不是爱的吻，那我就是被愚弄了。第二，你若真做我的朋友，我也绝不吝惜叫你爱人，绝不吝惜做你全心的朋友。至于第三个问题——告诉我，难道那事还缺时辰吗？」

她说到最后有些嗫嚅，他却说：「看哪，爱人，看今天大地多美！还有什么地方、什么时节比这更好？我们既彼此相爱，趁这甜美时节尽欢，岂不正好？如今这时节可是被我们的渴念糟蹋了些。」

「啊，爱人！」她羞答答地望着他说，「难道它真被那伤害不了我们的东西糟蹋了么？」

「听着！」他说，「这美好安宁、这闲适安稳，还能有多久？此时此地，大地在我们周围欢欣，没有人拦阻我们；明天也许一切都变样。想想吧，亲爱的，一个钟头之前，那怪物若把你撕了、杀了，咱们还不曾相拥而眠呢！」

===Original===

“Alas!” she said, “and had I lain in thine arms an hundred times, or an hundred times an hundred, should not the world be barren to me, wert thou gone from it, and that could never more be? But thou friend, thou well-beloved, fain were I to do thy will that thou mightest be the happier﻿ ﻿… and I withal. And if thou command it, be it so! Yet now should I tell thee all my thought, and it is on my mind, that for a many hundreds of years, yea, while our people were yet heathen, when a man should wed a maid all the folk knew of it, and were witnesses of the day and the hour thereof: now thou knowest that the time draws nigh when we may look for those messengers of the Innocent Folk, who come every spring to this cave to see if there be any whom they may speed on the way to the Well at the World’s End. Therefore if thou wilt (and not otherwise) I would abide their coming if it be not over long delayed; so that there may be others to witness our wedding besides God, and those his creatures who dwell in the wilderness. Yet shall all be as thou wilt.”

“How shall I not do after thy bidding?” said Ralph. “I will abide their coming: yet would that they were here today! And one thing I will pray of thee, that because of them thou wilt not forbear, or cause me to forbear, such kissing and caressing as is meet betwixt troth-plight lovers.”

She laughed and said: “Nay, why should I torment thee﻿ ﻿… or me? We will not tarry for this.” And therewith she took her arm about his neck and kissed him oft.

Then they said naught awhile, but sat listening happily to the song of the pairing birds. At last Ralph said: “What was it, beloved, that thou wert perchance to tell me concerning the thing that caused thine heart to see that thy betrothed, for whom thou wepst or seemedst to weep at the alehouse at Bourton Abbas, was of no avail to thee?”

She said: “It was the sight of thee; and I thought also how I might never be thine. For that I have sorrowed many a time since.”

Said Ralph: “I am young and unmighty, yet lo! I heal thy sorrow as if I were an exceeding mighty man. And now I tell thee that I am minded to go back with thee to Upmeads straightway; for love will prevail.”

===Chinese===

「唉！」她说，「就算我在你怀里躺过一百次、一百个一百次，你若从这世上去了、从此再不能回来，这世界对我岂不仍是荒漠一片？可是你，我的朋友、我的心爱，我巴不得顺从你的心意，好叫你更快活……也叫我快活。你若这样吩咐，那就这样吧！只是现在我该把心里的话都告诉你。我记着：千百年来——是的，远在我们的族人还是异教徒的时候——男人娶妻，全族的人都知道，都来见证那日子和时辰。你也知道，那些无辜子民的使者快要来了；他们每年春天都到这洞里来，看看有没有人需要他们送一程、去往世界尽头之泉。所以，如果你愿意——也只能是如果你愿意——我想等他们来，只要他们不来得太迟；这样，除了上帝和住在荒野里的他的造物之外，还可以有人见证我们的婚礼。不过，一切仍随你的心意。」

拉尔夫说：「我怎能不依你？我等他们来——只盼他们今天就到！还有一件事求你：别因为他们，你就约束自己、也不许我亲吻爱抚——订了婚的爱人之间，这些本是应当的。」

她笑道：「才不呢，我何苦折磨你……或者折磨我自己？这种事我们不必等。」说着她搂住他的脖颈，一次又一次地吻他。

两人静了好一会儿，快活地坐着听求偶的鸟儿歌唱。末了拉尔夫说：「爱人，你从前或许要告诉我一件事：是什么叫你的心明白，你在伯顿阿巴斯酒馆里为之哭泣——或者象是哭泣——的那个未婚夫，于你并无用处？」

她说：「是因为见到了你；我当时还想着，我永远做不成你的人。为这个，我后来伤心过许多回。」

拉尔夫说：「我年纪轻，又无权势；可是看哪！我医好了你的伤心，倒象个顶天立地的大英雄。现在我告诉你：我打算这就同你一起回阿普米兹去；因为爱情必胜。」

===Original===

“Nay,” she said, “that word is but from the teeth outwards; for thou knowest, as I do, that the perils of the homeward road shall overcome us, despite of love, if we have not drunk of the Well at the World’s End.”

Again they were silent awhile, but anon she arose to her feet and said: “Now must I needs dight victual for us twain; but first” (and she smiled on him withal), “how is it that thou hast not asked me if the beast did me any hurt? Art thou grown careless of me, now the wedding is so nigh?”

He said: “Nay, but could I not see thee that thou wert not hurt? There was no mark of blood upon thee, nor any stain at all.” Then she reddened, and said: “Ah, I forgot how keen-eyes thou art.” And she stood silent a little while, as he looked on her and loved her sweetness. Then he said: “I am exceeding full of joy, but my body is uneasy; so I will now go and skin that troll who went so nigh to slay thee, and break up the carcase, if thou wilt promise to abide about the door of the house, and have thy sword and the spear ready to hand, and to don thine helm and hauberk to boot.”

She laughed and said: “That were but strange attire for a cook-maid, Ralph, my friend; yet shall I do thy will, my lord and my love.”

Then went Ralph into the cave, and brought forth the armour and did it on her, and kissed her, and so went his ways to the carcase of the bear, which lay some two furlongs from their dwelling; and when he came to the quarry he fell to work, and was some time about it, so huge as the beast was. Then he hung the skin and the carcase on a tree of the grove, and went down to the river and washed him, and then went lightly homewards.

===Chinese===

她说：「不，这话不过是嘴上说说；你我都明白，若不喝过世界尽头之泉，归途的凶险终究会压倒我们——任凭爱情也无济于事。」

两人又沉默了一会儿；随后她站起身来说：「现在我得给咱们俩备饭了；不过先说一句——」（她朝他微笑）「你怎么不问问，那野兽伤着我没有？婚礼近了，你就这么不把我放在心上了？」

他说：「哪里话，我难道没看见你没受伤？你身上没有一点血痕，也没有一丝伤痕。」她脸红了，说：「啊，我忘了你眼尖。」她默默站了一小会儿，他望着她，爱她的娇美。然后他说：「我心里欢喜极了，身子却不得劲；我这就去把那头险些害了你性命的孽畜剥了皮、开膛破肉——你可要答应守在屋子门口，剑和长矛放在手边，还要戴上头盔、穿上锁子甲。」

她笑道：「拉尔夫，我的朋友，厨娘穿这一身可就怪了；不过我依你，我的夫君、我的爱人。」

拉尔夫进洞取出甲胄，替她穿上，吻了她，便朝熊尸走去——熊尸离住处约有两弗隆远。到了猎物跟前，他动手干活，那兽如此巨大，忙了好一阵子。他把皮和肉挂上林中一棵树，下河洗了洗，便轻快地回家去。

## XIV / 无辜之民的使者来了
===Original===

Now Come the Messengers of the Innocent Folk

But when he had come forth from the chestnut-grove, and could see the face of their house-rock clearly, he beheld new tidings; for there were folk before the door of the dwelling, and Ursula was standing amidst of them, for he could see the gleam of her armour; and with the men he could see also certain beasts of burden, and anon that these were oxen. So he hastened on to find what this might mean, and drew his sword as he went. But when he came up to the rock, he found there two young men and an elder, and they had with them five oxen, three for riding, and two sumpter beasts, laden: and Ursula and these men were talking together friendly; so that Ralph deemed that the newcomers must be the messengers of the Innocent Folk. They were goodly men all three, somewhat brown of skin, but well fashioned, and of smiling cheerful countenance, well knit, and tall. The elder had a long white beard, but his eye was bright, and his hand firm and smooth. They were all clad in white woollen raiment, and bore no armour, but each had an axe with a green stone blade, curiously tied to the heft, and each of the young men carried a strong bow and a quiver of arrows.

Ralph greeted the men, and bade them sit down on the toft and eat a morsel; they took his greeting kindly, and sat down, while Ursula went into the cave to fetch them matters for their victual, and there was already venison roasting at the fire on the toft, in the place where they were wont to cook their meat. So then came Ursula forth from the cave, and served the newcomers and Ralph of such things as she had, and they ate and drank together; and none said aught of their errand till they had done their meat, but they talked together pleasantly about the spring, and the blossoms of the plain and the mountain, and the wild things that dwelt thereabout.

But when the meal was over, the newcomers rose to their feet, and bowed before Ralph and Ursula, and the elder took up the word and said: “Ye fair people, have ye any errand in the wilderness, or are ye chance-comers who have strayed thus far, and know not how to return?”

“Father,” said Ralph, “we have come a long way on an errand of life or death; for we seek the **Well** at the **World’s End**. And see ye the token thereof, the pair of beads which we bear, either of us, and the fashion whereof ye know.”

===Chinese===

可他刚走出栗树林，一眼望见家中岩壁的正面，便看见了新的动静：居所门前站着一些人，厄休拉正在他们中间——他看得见她甲胄的闪光；那些人身边还有些驮兽，转眼看清是牛。他加快脚步赶过去看个究竟，边走边拔出剑来。待他走到岩石跟前，发现那里是两个年轻人和一位老者，带着五头牛：三头坐骑，两头驮畜，驮着东西；厄休拉正和他们亲热地交谈。拉尔夫于是断定，来者必定是无辜之民的使者。三人都是仪表堂堂的汉子，肤色微棕，但体格匀称，眉目开朗，笑容可掬，身板结实，个子高挑。老者蓄着长长的白须，目光炯炯，手劲沉稳，肌肤却还平滑。三人都穿着白色呢衣，不披甲胄，但各有一柄斧子，斧刃是绿玉石做的，以精巧的手法缚在柄上；两个年轻人还各背一张强弓和一袋箭。

拉尔夫向他们致意，请他们到土墩上坐下一同吃点东西；他们欣然接受了问候坐下，厄休拉进洞去取吃食——土墩上他们惯常做饭的地方，火堆上正烤着鹿肉。随后厄休拉从洞中出来，把手头有的东西端给客人和拉尔夫，大家一同吃喝；饭吃完之前谁也没提来意，只是愉快地谈着春天，谈平原上和山间的花，谈住在这一带的野物。

饭后，来客们站起身，向拉尔夫和厄休拉躬身行礼，老者开口道：“二位佳客，你们在这荒野中是有使命在身呢，还是偶然走迷了路、误到此地不知归途的过客？”

“老人家，”拉尔夫说，“我们远道而来，身负生死攸关的使命；我们寻找的是**世界尽头之泉**。请看凭信——我们二人各戴着一串珠子，那样式你们是认得的。”

===Original===

Then the elder bowed to them again, and said: “It is well; then is this our errand with you, to be your way-leaders as far as the House of the Sorceress, where ye shall have other help. Will ye set out on the journey today? In one hour shall we be ready.”

“Nay,” said Ralph, “we will not depart till tomorrow morn, if it may be so. Therewith I bid you sit down and rest you, while ye hearken a word which I have to say to you.”

So they sat down again, and Ralph arose and took Ursula by the hand, and stood with her before the elder, and said: “This maiden, who is my fellow-farer in the Quest, I desire to wed this same night, and she also desireth me: therefore I would have you as witnesses hereto. But first ye shall tell us if our wedding and the knowing each other carnally shall be to our hurt in the Quest; for if that be so, then shall we bridle our desires and perform our Quest in their despite.”

The old man smiled upon them kindly, and said: “Nay, son, we hear not that it shall be the worse for you in any wise that ye shall become one flesh; and right joyful it is to us, not only that we have found folk who seek to the Well at the World’s End, but also that there is such love as I perceive there is betwixt such goodly and holy folk as ye be. For hither we come year by year according to the behest that we made to the fairest woman of the world, when she came back to us from the Well at the World’s End, and it is many and many a year ago since we found any seekers after the Well dwelling here. Therefore have we the more joy in you. And we have brought hither matters good for you, as raiment, and meal, and wine, on our sumpter-beasts; therefore as ye have feasted us this morning, so shall we feast you this even. And if ye will, we shall build for you in the grove yonder such a bower as we build for our own folk on the night of the wedding.”

===Chinese===

老者又向他们躬身行礼，说：“这就对了；那么我们此来为你们办的差事，就是给你们引路，一直送到妖巫之屋，在那里你们会得到别的帮助。你们今天就动身吗？一个钟头后我们就可备好。”

“不，”拉尔夫说，“若是可行，我们要到明天早晨才动身。且请你们坐下歇歇，听我说一句话。”

他们重新坐下，拉尔夫起身拉住厄休拉的手，同她一起站到老者面前，说：“这位姑娘是我的求索同伴，我想就在今夜与她成婚，她也属意于我：因此我想请你们做这场婚礼的见证。但首先请你们告诉我们，我们的结合、夫妻之实的相知，是否会损害我们的求索；若是会，我们便勒住这份欲望，宁可逆着它也要完成求索。”

老人慈祥地对他们微笑，说：“不会的，孩子，我们从没听说你们结为一体会给你们带来任何妨害；让我们欢喜的不单是找到了寻找世界尽头之泉的人，还因为在你们这样美好圣洁的人儿之间，竟有着我所见到的这般深情。因为我们年年到这里来，这是当年世上最美的女子从世界尽头之泉回到我们身边时，我们对她许下的诺言；算来已有许多许多年，我们不曾在这里见到寻泉人的踪迹了。所以遇见你们，我们格外欢喜。我们用驮畜给你们带来了于你们有用的东西：衣裳、面粉，还有酒；早晨你们款待了我们，今晚就让我们来回请你们。你们若愿意，我们还可以在那边树林里为你们搭一座凉棚，就像我们为自己人婚礼之夜搭的那样。”

===Original===

Ralph yeasaid this, and thanked them. So then the elder cried: “Up, my sons, and show your deftness to these dear friends!” Then the young men arose, naught loth, and when they had hoppled their oxen and taken the burdens from off them, they all went down the meadow together into the chestnut grove, and they fell to and cut willow boughs, and suchlike wood, and drave stakes and wove the twigs together; and Ralph and Ursula worked with them as they bade, and they were all very merry together: because for those two wanderers it was a great delight to see the faces of the children of men once more after so many months, and to hold converse with them; while for their part the young men marvelled at Ursula’s beauty, and the pith and goodliness of Ralph.

By then it was nigh evening they had made a very goodly wattled bower, and roofed it with the skins that were in the cave, and hung it about with garlands, and strewn flowers on the floor thereof. And when all was done they went back to the toft before the rock-chamber, where the elder had opened the loads, and had taken meal thence, and was making cakes at the fire. And there was wine there in well-hooped kegs, and wooden cups fairly carven, and raiment of fine white wool for those twain, broidered in strange but beauteous fashion with the feathers of bright-hued birds.

So then were those twain arrayed for the bridal; and the meat was dight and the cups filled, and they sat down on the grassy toft a little before sunset, and feasted till the night was come, and was grown all light with the moon; and then Ralph rose up, and took Ursula’s hand, and they stood before the elder, and bade him and the young men bear witness that they were wedded: then those twain kissed the newcomers and departed to their bridal bower hand in hand through the freshness of the night.

===Chinese===

拉尔夫应允了，向他们道谢。老者便喊道：“起来，孩子们，在这两位亲爱的朋友面前显显你们的手艺！”两个年轻人巴不得地起身，拴好牛，卸下驮子，大家一起下了草场，走进栗树林；他们动手砍下柳枝之类的木料，打桩编条，拉尔夫和厄休拉也依着吩咐一起动手；大伙儿干得欢天喜地：对那两个流浪者来说，隔了这么多个月又能见到人类的面孔，同他们说话，实在是莫大的快乐；而两个年轻人则惊叹厄休拉的美貌，惊叹拉尔夫的精壮英伟。

将近黄昏时，他们已搭好一座十分美观的枝条凉棚，用洞里的兽皮做了顶，四周挂上花环，地上铺满了鲜花。一切停当后，他们回到岩室前的土墩上；老者已打开驮包，取出面粉，正在火边做饼。那里还有箍得结结实实的桶装美酒，雕工精美的木杯，以及给两人备下的细白呢衣裳，用色彩斑斓的鸟羽绣着奇异而美妙的花纹。

随后两人换上了婚礼的装束；饭菜备好，杯子斟满，日落前不久，他们在青草茵茵的土墩上坐下，一直欢宴到夜幕降临，月光洒满大地；然后拉尔夫站起身，牵起厄休拉的手，站到老者面前，请他同两个年轻人见证他们结为夫妻：随后两人吻别了来客，手拉着手，穿过清凉的夜色，往他们的新婚凉棚去了。

## XV / 他们来到无辜之民的土地
===Original===

They Come to the Land of the Innocent Folk

When it was morning they speedily gat them ready for the road, whereas they had little to take with them; so they departed joyously, howbeit both Ralph and Ursula felt rather love than loathing for their winter abode. The day was yet young when they went their ways. Their horses and all their gear were a great wonder to the young men, for they had seen no such beasts before: but the elder said that once in his young days he had led a man to the Well who was riding a horse and was clad in knightly array.

So they went by ways which were nowise dreadful, though they were void of menfolk, and in three days’ time they were come out of the mountains, and in three more the said mountains were to behold but a cloud behind them, and the land was grown goodly, with fair valleys and little hills, though still they saw no men, and forsooth they went leisurely, for oxen are but slow-going nags. But when they were gone eight days from the Valley of Sweet-chestnuts, they came across a flock of uncouth-looking sheep on a green hillside, and four folk shepherding them, two carles to wit, and two queans, like to their way-leaders, but scarce so goodly, and ruder of raiment. These men greeted them kindly, and yet with more worship than fellowship, and they marvelled exceedingly at their horses and weapons. Thence they passed on, and the next day came into a wide valley, well-grassed and watered, and wooded here and there; moreover there were cots scattered about it. There and thenceforth they met men a many, both carles and queans, and sheep and neat in plenty, and they passed by garths wherein the young corn was waxing, and vineyards on the hillsides, where the vines were beginning to grow green. The land seemed as goodly as might be, and all the folk they met were kind, if somewhat over reverent.

On the evening of that day they came into the town of that folk, which was but simple, wholly unfenced for war, and the houses but low, and not great. Yet was there naught of filth or famine, nor any poverty or misery; and the people were merry-faced and well-liking, and clad goodly after their fashion in white woollen cloth or frieze. All the people of the town were come forth to meet them, for runners had gone before them, and they stood on either side of the way murmuring greetings, and with their heads bent low in reverence.

===Chinese===

清晨一到，他们便迅速收拾停当上路，反正要带的东西不多；于是他们欢欢喜喜地启程了——不过拉尔夫和厄休拉对这座过冬的居所，与其说厌弃，不如说怀着眷恋。上路时天色尚早。他们的马匹和全部行头让两个年轻人啧啧称奇，因为他们从没见过这样的牲口：老者却说，他年轻的时候，曾经引过一个骑马、身着骑士装束的人去泉水那里。

他们一路走去，道路毫无凶险，只是不见人烟；三天后他们出了山，再过三天，回头望去，群山已只剩天边一抹云影，大地渐渐变得美好，山谷秀丽，丘陵低缓，却仍旧见不到人——他们走得也确实从容，因为牛实在不是快脚的牲口。离开甜栗谷八天之后，他们在一片青翠的山坡上遇见一群模样粗陋的绵羊，四个牧人看护着：两个汉子，两个女子，长得同引路人相像，只是没那么俊美，衣衫也粗些。这些人和善地向他们问好，只是敬多于亲，对他们的马匹兵器惊叹不已。他们继续前行，第二天进入一条宽阔的山谷，水草丰美，间或有树木点缀，谷中散布着农舍。从这里开始，他们见到许多的人，男女都有，羊群牛群也不少；他们经过一座座围田，田里的幼麦正在生长，还经过山坡上的葡萄园，藤蔓开始泛绿。这地方美好得无可挑剔，遇到的所有人都很和善，只是敬畏得有些过头。

当天傍晚，他们来到那个民族的城镇。城池十分朴素，全无防御工事，房屋低矮，也不宏大。然而这里没有污秽，没有饥馑，没有贫穷和困苦；人们个个满面喜色，丰神俊朗，按他们的样式穿着白色呢布或粗呢的漂亮衣裳。全镇的人统统出来迎接，因为早有报信的人跑到了前头；人们站在道路两旁，低声致意，深深躬首，满怀敬畏。

===Original===

Thus rode Ralph and Ursula up to the door of the Temple, or Mote-house, or Guesthouse, for it was all these, a house great, and as fair as they knew how to make it. Before the door thereof were standing the elders of the Folk; and when they drew rein, the eldest and most reverend of these came forth and spake in a cheerful voice, yet solemnly: “Welcome and thrice welcome to the Seekers after length of days and happy times, and the loving-kindness of the Folks of the Earth!”

Then all the elders gathered about them, and bade them light down and be at rest amongst them, and they made much of them and brought them into the Mote-house, wherein were both women and men fair and stately, and the men took Ralph by the hand and the women Ursula, and brought them into chambers where they bathed them and did off their wayfaring raiment, and clad them in white woollen gowns of web exceeding fine, and fragrant withal. Then they crowned them with flowers, and led them back into the hall, whereas now was much folk gathered, and they set them down on a dais as though they had been kings, or rather gods; and when they beheld them there so fair and lovely, they cried out for joy of them, and bade them hail oft and oft.

There then were they feasted by that kind folk, and when meat was done certain youths and maidens fell to singing songs very sweetly; and the words of the songs were simple and harmless, and concerning the fairness of the earth and the happy loves of the creatures that dwell therein.

Thereafter as the night aged, they were shown to a sleeping chamber, which albeit not richly decked, or plenished with precious things, was most dainty clean, and sweet smelling, and strewn with flowers, so that the night was sweet to them in a chamber of love.

===Chinese===

拉尔夫和厄休拉就这样骑马来到神庙——或者说议事堂、客栈，因为它兼有这几种用途——的门前：这是一座大屋，造得尽他们所能地精美。门前站着这个民族的长老们；他们勒住缰绳，其中最年长、最受尊敬的一位走上前来，用欢快而庄重的声音说：“欢迎，万分欢迎这两位追寻长寿岁月、幸福时光和大地诸族慈爱之情的寻泉人！”

众长老随即围拢过来，请他们下马安歇；大家对他们殷勤备至，把他们引进议事堂。堂内男女个个俊美端庄，男人们牵着拉尔夫的手，女人们牵着厄休拉的手，领他们进到厢房，替他们沐浴，脱去旅途的衣装，给他们穿上织得极其细软、还带着香气的白色呢袍。然后为他们戴上花冠，又领他们回到大厅——这时厅里已聚了许多人——请他们在上座就坐，仿佛他们是君王，不如说是神明；众人望着坐在那里的他们那样俊美可爱，喜得高声欢呼，一遍又一遍地向他们致敬。

随后，这个善良的民族设宴款待他们；饭毕，几个青年男女唱起歌来，歌声十分甜美；歌词纯朴无邪，唱的是大地的秀美，和世间生灵幸福的爱恋。

夜深之后，有人引他们去寝室；那屋子虽然没有华贵的陈设和珍奇之物，却极其雅洁，满室生香，地上撒满花朵——在这间爱巢里，他们的这一夜过得甜甜蜜蜜。

## XVI / 十六
===Original===

They Come to the House of the Sorceress

On the morrow the kind people delayed them little, though they sorrowed for their departure, and before noon were their old way-leaders ready for them; and the old man and his two grandsons (for such they were) were much honoured of the simple people for their way-leading of the Heavenly Folk; for so they called Ralph and Ursula. So they gat them to the way in suchlike guise as before, only they had with them five sumpter oxen instead of two; for the old man told them that not only was their way longer, but also they must needs pass through a terrible waste, wherein was naught for their avail, neither man, nor beast, nor herb. Even so they found it as he said; for after the first day’s ride from the town they came to the edge of this same waste, and on the fourth day were deep in the heart of it: a desert it was, rather rocky and stony and sandy than mountainous, though they had hills to cross also: withal there was but little water there, and that foul and stinking. Long lasted this waste, and Ralph thought indeed that it had been hard to cross, had not their way-leaders been; therefore he made marks and signs by the wayside, and took note of the bearings of rocks and mounds against the day of return.

Twelve days they rode this waste, and on the thirteenth it began to mend somewhat, and there was a little grass, and sweet waters, and they saw ahead the swelling hills of a great woodland, albeit they had to struggle through marshland and low scrubby thicket for a day longer, or ever they got to the aforesaid trees, which at first were naught but pines; but these failed in a while, and they rode a grass waste nearly treeless, but somewhat well watered, where they gat them good store of venison. Thereafter they came on woods of oak and sweet-chestnut, with here and there a beechwood.

===Chinese===

他们来到女巫之屋

次日，善良的人们虽为他们的离去难过，却没有多加挽留；不到正午，原先那几位带路人已为他们备好。老人和他的两个孙子（正是这层关系）因给天人带路，在纯朴的人们中间备受尊荣——天人便是他们对拉尔夫和厄休拉的称呼。于是他们照旧启程，只是驮畜由两头牛换成了五头；因为老人告诉他们，此去不但路程更长，还须穿过一片可怕的荒原，那里于人无益，无兽、无草。果然如他所说：离开城后第一天的路程，他们便到了这片荒原的边缘，第四天已深入它的腹地。那是一片沙漠，与其说多山，不如说多岩、多石、多沙——虽然也有山丘要翻越；此外那里水极少，而且又臭又浑。这片荒原走了很久；拉尔夫心想，若不是有带路人，实在难以穿越；因此他在路旁做下记号，记下岩石和土冈的方位，以备归程之用。

他们在荒原上走了十二天，第十三天地面渐渐好转，有了些草，水也甜了；他们望见前方一片大林地的隆起山丘，只是还须在沼泽和低矮的灌木丛中挣扎一天，才能到得上述的树林——起初那不过是些松树；不久松林尽了，又走一片几乎无树的草地荒原，但水源还算充足，他们在那里猎得了不少野味。此后便来到橡树和甜栗的树林，间或一片山毛榉。

===Original===

Long and long they rode the woodland, but it was hard on May when they entered it, and it was pleasant therein, and what with one thing, what with another, they had abundant livelihood there. Yet was June at its full when at last they came within sight of the House of the Sorceress, on the hottest of a fair afternoon. And it was even as Ralph had seen it pictured in the arras of the hall of the Castle of Abundance; a little house built after the fashion of houses in his own land of the west; the thatch was trim, and the windows and doors were unbroken, and the garth was whole, and the goats feeding therein, and the wheat was tall and blossoming in the little closes, whereas he had looked to see all broken down and wild, and as to the house, a mere grass-grown heap, or at the most a broken gable fast crumbling away.

Then waxed his heart sore with the memory of that passed time, and the sweetness of his short-lived love, though he refrained him all he might: yet forsooth Ursula looked on him anxiously, so much his face was changed by the thoughts of his heart.

But the elder of the way-leaders saw that he was moved, and deemed that he was wondering at that house so trim and orderly amidst the wildwood, so he said: “Here also do we after our behest to that marvellous and lovely Lady, that we suffer not this house to go to ruin: ever are some of our folk here, and every year about this season we send two or more to take the places of those who have dwelt in the House yearlong: so ever is there someone to keep all things trim. But as to strangers, I have never in my life seen any Seeker of the Well herein, save once, and that was an old hoar man like to me, save that he was feebler in all wise than I be.”

Now Ralph heard him talking, yet noted his words but little; for it was with him as if all the grief of heart which he had penned back for so long a while swelled up within him and burst its bounds; and he turned toward Ursula and their eyes met, and she looked shy and anxious on him and he might no longer refrain himself, but put his hands to his face (for they had now drawn rein at the garth-gate) and brake out a weeping, and wept long for the friend whose feet had worn that path so often, and whose heart, though she were dead, had brought them thither for their thriving; and for love and sorrow of him Ursula wept also.

===Chinese===

他们在林中走了很久很久；进林时已近五月，林中景致宜人，加上这样那样的出产，生计绰绰有余。待终于望见女巫之屋时，六月已圆，那是一个晴好午间最炎热的时分。那屋子正如拉尔夫在丰饶堡大厅的挂毯上见过的一样：一座小屋，样式如同他西部家乡的房屋；茅草修得整整齐齐，门窗完好无损，园圃齐整，山羊在里面吃草，小块的围地里麦子长得高高的，正在抽穗开花。他原以为会见到一片残破荒芜，屋子呢，至多是一堆长满荒草的废墟，或是一堵正在崩塌的断山墙。

旧日时光和那段短促爱情的甜美涌上心头，他心里痛楚起来，尽管极力克制；厄休拉却不安地望着他，因为他心中的思绪已使面色大变。

带路人中的老人见他那般激动，只当他是在惊异荒林之中竟有这样齐整的宅子，便说：「我们遵着那位奇妙可爱的夫人的嘱托，在这里也不许这座屋子倾颓：我们的族人常年有人在此，每年这个时节，我们都会派两三个或更多的人来，接替在屋里住满一年的人，所以总有人把一切收拾得妥妥帖帖。至于外人，我平生在这里只见过一位寻泉客，仅此一回；那是个白发苍苍的老人，与我相仿，只是处处比我衰弱。」

拉尔夫听见他说话，却几乎没听进那些话；只觉得久来强压在心头的悲伤涨了起来，冲破了堤岸；他转向厄休拉，两人目光相遇，她羞怯而不安地望着他；他再也忍不住，双手掩面（这时他们已在园门口勒住马），放声哭了出来，久久哭泣——为那位曾经无数次踏熟这条小径的朋友；她虽然死了，她的心却引他们来到这里，让他们得享兴盛。出于对他的爱与哀伤，厄休拉也哭了。

===Original===

But the old man and his grandsons turned their heads away from his weeping, and got off their horses, and went up to the house-door, whereby were now standing a carle and a quean of their people. But Ralph slowly gat off his horse and stood by Ursula who was on the ground already, but would not touch her, for he was ashamed. But she looked on him kindly and said: “Dear friend, there is no need for shame; for though I be young, I know how grievous it is when the dead that we have loved come across our ways, and we may not speak to them, nor they to us. So I will but bid thee be comforted and abide in thy love for the living and the dead.” His tears brake out again at that word, for he was but young, and for a while there was a lull in the strife that had beset his days. But after a little he looked up, and dashed the tears from his eyes and smiled on Ursula and said: “The tale she told me of this place, the sweetness of it came back upon me, and I might not forbear.” She said: “O friend, thou art kind, and I love thee.”

So then they joined hands and went through the garth together, and up to the door, where stood the wardens, who, when they saw them turning thither, came speedily down the path to them, and would have knelt in worship to them; but they would not suffer it, but embraced and kissed them, and thanked them many times for their welcome. The said wardens, both carle and quean, were goodly folk of middle age, stalwart, and kind of face.

So then they went into the house together, and entered into the selfsame chamber, where of old the Lady of Abundance had sickened for fear of the Sorceress sitting naked at her spell-work.

===Chinese===

老人和他的孙子们把脸从他哭泣的方向转开，下了马，向屋门走去——门口已站着一男一女两个他们的族人。拉尔夫缓缓下马，站到厄休拉身旁——她早已下了地——却不敢碰她，因为他心里羞愧。她温柔地望着他，说：「亲爱的朋友，不必羞愧；我虽然年轻，却知道那是怎样难堪：我们爱过的死者横在路上，我们不能对他们说话，他们也不能对我们说。我只想劝你宽心，把对生者与死者的爱都守在心里。」听了这话他的眼泪又涌出来，因为他毕竟还年轻；而这一刻，连日缠绕他的纷争也有了个间歇。过了一会儿他抬起头，抹去眼泪，对厄休拉笑了笑，说：「她从前给我讲这地方的故事，那份甜美又涌上心头，我忍不住。」她说：「啊，朋友，你真好，我爱你。」

于是两人携起手，一同穿过园圃，向屋门走去。门口守着屋子的那两人见他们转来，急忙顺着小径迎上前，要跪拜他们；他们却不肯受，反而拥抱亲吻他们，为这番欢迎再三道谢。那两个守屋人，一男一女，都是中年良善之辈，身强力壮，面容和善。

随后他们一同进屋，走进的正是当年那间屋子——丰饶夫人在那里因惧怕赤身裸体作法的女巫而生过一场大病。

===Original===

Great joy they made together, and the wardens set meat and drink before the guests, and they ate and drank and were of good cheer. But the elder who had brought them from Chestnut-dale said: “Dear friends, I have told you that these two young men are my grandchildren, and they are the sons of this man and woman whom ye see; for the man is my son. And so it is, that amongst us the care of the Quest of the Well at the World’s End hath for long been the heritage of our blood, going with us from father to son. Therefore is it naught wonderful, though I have been sundry times at this house, and have learned about the place all that may be learned. For my father brought me hither when I was yet a boy; that time it was that I saw the last man of whom we know for sure that he drank of the Water of the Well, and he was that old hoar man like unto me, but, as I said, far weaker in all wise; but when he came back to us from the Well he was strong and stalwart, and a better man than I am now; and I heard him tell his name to my father, that he was called the Sage of Swevenham.”

Ralph looked on Ursula and said: “Yea, father, and it was through him that we had our lore concerning the way hither; and it was he that bade us abide your coming in the rock-house of the Vale of Sweet-chestnuts.”

“Then he is alive still,” said the elder. Said Ralph: “Yea, and as fair and strong an old man as ye may lightly see.” “Yea, yea,” said the elder, “and yet fifty years ago his course seemed run.”

Then said Ralph: “Tell me, father, have none of your own folk sought to the Well at the World’s End?” “Nay, none,” said the elder. Said Ralph: “That is strange, whereas ye are so nigh thereto, and have such abundant lore concerning the way.”

===Chinese===

众人一起欢叙，守屋人在客人面前摆上酒肉，大家吃喝快活。从栗谷送他们来的老人说：「亲爱的朋友，我告诉过你们，这两个年轻人是我的孙子，是你们眼前这一男一女的儿子——那男人是我的儿子。事情就是这样：在我们中间，照管世界尽头之泉探寻之旅，久已是我们血脉的世传，父子相承。所以我来过这屋子好几回、把这地方能学的都学了，一点也不奇怪。我父亲带我到这里来时，我还是个孩子；正是那一次，我见到了我们所确知喝过泉水的最后一人；他就是那个和我相仿的白发老人，但如我所说，处处比我衰弱得多；可他从泉边回到我们那里时，强壮魁伟，比现在的我还要强健；我听他对我父亲通报姓名，说他叫斯韦文汉的贤者。」

拉尔夫望了厄休拉一眼，说：「是啊，老丈，我们得以来此的路途学问，正是得自他；是他嘱咐我们在甜栗之谷的石屋里等候你们到来。」

「那么他还活着。」老人说。拉尔夫说：「活着，还是一位你们轻易见得到的健旺强壮的老人。」「是啊，是啊，」老人说，「可五十年前，他的寿数好象就到头了。」

拉尔夫又问：「老丈，告诉我，你们本族的人就没有去寻过世界尽头之泉吗？」「没有，一个也没有。」老人说。拉尔夫说：「这就怪了，你们离得这么近，又有这么完备的路途学问。」

===Original===

“Son,” said the elder, “true it is that the water of that Well shall cause a man to thrive in all ways, and to live through many generations of men, maybe, in honour and good-liking; but it may not keep any man alive forever; for so have the Gods given us the gift of death lest we weary of life. Now our folk live well and hale, and without the sickness and pestilence, such as I have heard oft befall folk in other lands: even as I heard the Sage of Swevenham say, and I wondered at his words. Of strife and of war also we know naught: nor do we desire aught which we may not easily attain to. Therefore we live long, and we fear the Gods if we should strive to live longer, lest they should bring upon us war and sickness, and overweening desire, and weariness of life. Moreover it is little that all of us should seek to the Well at the World’s End; and those few that sought and drank should be stronger and wiser than the others, and should make themselves earthly gods, and, maybe, should torment the others of us and make their lives a very burden to be borne. Of such matters are there tales current amongst us that so it hath been of yore and in other lands; and ill it were if such times came back upon us.”

Ralph hung his head and was silent; for the joy of the Quest seemed dying out as the old man’s words dropped slowly from his mouth. But he smiled upon Ralph and went on: “But for you, guests, it is otherwise, for ye of the World beyond the Mountains are stronger and more godlike than we, as all tales tell; and ye wear away your lives desiring that which ye may scarce get; and ye set your hearts on high things, desiring to be masters of the very Gods. Therefore ye know sickness and sorrow, and oft ye die before your time, so that ye must depart and leave undone things which ye deem ye were born to do; which to all men is grievous. And because of all this ye desire healing and thriving, whether good come of it, or ill. Therefore ye do but right to seek to the Well at the World’s End, that ye may the better accomplish that which behoveth you, and that ye may serve your fellows and deliver them from the thralldom of those that be strong and unwise and unkind, of whom we have heard strange tales.”

Ralph reddened as he spake, and Ursula looked on him anxiously, but that talk dropped for the present, and they fell to talking of lighter and more familiar matters.

===Chinese===

「孩子，」老人说，「那泉水确实能叫人事事兴旺，也许还能让人体面安康地活过好几代人；可它不能叫任何人永生不死；诸神正是因此才把死亡赐给我们，免得我们对生命厌倦。我们的族人活得康健，没有疾病瘟疫——我常听说别处的人常遭这些灾殃，正如我听斯韦文汉的贤者说过的那样，我当时就对他的话称奇。争斗和战争我们也一无所知；我们也不贪求任何不易得到的东西。所以我们长寿；而我们若想活得更长，便怕诸神降下战争、疾病、骄纵的贪欲和对生命的厌倦。再说，我们若人人都去寻世界尽头之泉，也很不妥：寻到喝过的那几个，就会比旁人更强更智，自命为人间的神明，说不定还要折磨我们其余的人，把他们的生命变成一副重担。这类事，我们中间流传的故事说，古时、在别处，就是这样的；那样的时代若再回来，就糟了。」

拉尔夫低下头，默默无言；随着老人的话一字一字缓缓落下，探寻的欢欣仿佛正在熄灭。老人却朝他微微一笑，接着说：「至于你们，客人，却是另一回事：山外世界的人比我们强大、比我们更近神明，一切故事都这么说；你们把生命耗在渴求难以到手的东西上；你们把心放在高处，连诸神也想驾驭。所以你们有病痛忧愁，常常未尽天年而死，撇下你们认为生来要做的事没有做完——这对谁都是痛事。正因为这一切，你们渴望疗治与兴旺，不论它带来善还是恶。所以你们去寻世界尽头之泉并没有错：好教你们更圆满地成就分内之事，好教你们服务同类，把他们从那些强大、愚蠢又冷酷者的奴役中解救出来——关于这类人，我们听过种种奇怪的故事。」

他说这些话时拉尔夫脸红了，厄休拉不安地望着他；这个话题眼下就此打住，他们转而谈起轻松些的家常来。

===Original===

Thereafter they wandered about the woods with the wardens and the way-leaders, and the elder brought them to the ancient altar in the wood whereon the Sorceress had offered up the goat; and the howe of the woman dight with the necklace of the Quest whom the Lady found dead in the snow; and the place nigh the house where the Sorceress used to torment her thrall that was afterwards the Lady of Abundance; yea, and they went further afield till they came to the Vale of Lore, and the Heath above it where they met, the King’s Son and the Lady. All these and other places were now become as hallowed ground to the Innocent People, and to Ralph no less. In the house, moreover, was a fair ark wherein they kept matters which had belonged to the Lady, as her shoes and her smock, wrapped in goodly cloth amidst well-smelling herbs; and these things they worshipped as folk do with relics of the saints. In another ark also they showed the seekers a book wherein was written lore concerning the Well, and the way thereto. But of this book had the Sage forewarned Ralph and his mate, and had bidden them look to it that they should read in it, and no otherwhere than at that ancient altar in the wood, they two alone, and clad in suchlike gear as they wore when they hearkened to his reading by his hermitage. And so it was that they found the due raiment in the ark along with the book. Therefore day after day betimes in the morning they bore the said book to the altar and read therein, till they had learned much wisdom.

Thus they did for eight days, and on the ninth they rested and were merry with their hosts: but on the tenth day they mounted their horses and said farewell, and departed by the ways they had learned of, they two alone. And they had with them bread and meal, as much as they might bear, and water-skins moreover, that they might fill them at the last sweet water before they came to the waterless desert.

===Chinese===

此后他们同守屋人和带路人一起在林中各处游逛；老人领他们去看林中那座古祭坛——女巫当年曾在上面献祭山羊；去看那座坟莹——葬着佩戴探寻项链、被夫人发现死在雪里的女子；去看屋旁那处地方——女巫从前在那里折磨她的女奴，那女奴后来成了丰饶夫人；是的，他们还走得更远，直到学问之谷和谷上方的那片荒原——王子与夫人当年相会之处。所有这些地方以及其他地方，如今在无辜子民眼中都成了圣地，在拉尔夫眼中也不例外。屋里还有一口漂亮的柜子，里面收藏着夫人的遗物，如她的鞋子和衬衣，用贵重的布裹着，衬着香草；这些物件他们奉若圣徒的遗物。在另一口柜子里，他们还给两位寻泉客看了一本书，书里写着关于那泉与路途的学问。这本书贤者早对拉尔夫和他的同伴预先叮嘱过，嘱咐他们务必只在林中那座古祭坛前读，只许他们两人独读，并且要穿在他们隐庐听读时所穿的那类衣裳。果然，他们在这口柜子里连书带应穿的衣裳都找到了。于是一天又一天，他们一早把那本书捧到祭坛前诵读，直到学得了许多智慧。

这样过了八天，第九天他们歇息，与主人们一同欢乐；第十天他们上马道别，循所学得的路径出发了，只他们两人。他们带了面包和面粉，能带多少带多少，还带了水囊，好在到达无水的荒漠之前，在最后一处甜水泉灌满。

## XVII / 他们穿过林地来到干渴的荒漠
===Original===

They Come Through the Woodland to the Thirsty Desert

So they ride their ways, and when they were come well into the wildwood past the house, and had spoken but few words to each other, Ralph put forth his hand, and stayed Ursula, and they gat off their horses under a great-limbed oak, and did off their armour, and sat down on the greensward there, and loved each other dearly, and wept for joy of their pain and travail and love. And afterwards, as they sat side by side leaning up against the great oak-bole, Ralph spake and said: “Now are we two once again all alone in the uttermost parts of the earth, and belike we are not very far from the Well at the World’s End; and now I have bethought me that if we gain that which we seek for, and bear back our lives to our own people, the day may come when we are grown old, for as young as we may seem, that we shall be as lonely then as we are this hour, and that the folk round about us shall be to us as much and no more than these trees and the wild things that dwell amongst them.”

She looked on him and laughed as one over-happy, and said: “Thou runnest forward swiftly to meet trouble, beloved! But I say that well will it be in those days if I love the folk then as well as now I love these trees and the wild things whose house they are.”

And she rose up therewith and threw her arms about the oak-bole and kissed its ruggedness, while Ralph as he lay kissed the sleekness of her feet. And there came a robin hopping over the leaves anigh them, for in that wood most of the creatures, knowing not man, were tame to him, and feared the horses of those twain more than their riders. And now as Ursula knelt to embrace Ralph with one hand, she held out the other to the said robin who perched on her wrist, and sat there as a hooded falcon had done, and fell to whistling his sweet notes, as if he were a-talking to those newcomers: then Ursula gave him a song-reward of their broken meat, and he flew up and perched on her shoulder, and nestled up against her cheek, and she laughed happily and said: “Lo you, sweet, have not the wild things understood my words, and sent this fair messenger to foretell us all good?”

“It is good,” said Ralph laughing, “yet the oak tree hath not spoken yet, despite of all thy kissing: and lo there goes thy friend the robin, now thou hast no more meat to give him.”

===Chinese===

于是他们骑马上路；走过那座屋子、深入莽林之后，彼此几乎没说几句话，拉尔夫便伸出手，让厄休拉停下来。两人在一棵枝干参天的橡树下下了马，卸下甲胄，在那片绿草地上坐下，深深地彼此相爱，为他们的苦难、艰辛与爱情喜极而泣。

过后，两人并肩倚着大橡树干坐着，拉尔夫开口道：“如今我们又两人独处在这天涯海角了，想来离世界尽头之泉已经不远；可我此刻想到，纵使我们求得所求，把生命带回给我们的族人，将来我们终有老去的一天——任凭眼下显得多么年轻——到那时，我们会同此刻一样孤独，身边的世人于我们，也不过同这些树木和林中的野物一样，仅此而已。”

她望着他，像幸福过了头的人似的笑了，说：“你迎着烦恼跑得可真快，亲爱的人！可我说，到那时只要我还能像现在爱这些树木和以林为家的野物一样爱世人，那就很好。”

说着她站起身，张开双臂抱住橡树干，吻着它粗硬的树皮；躺着的拉尔夫则吻着她柔滑的双足。一只知更鸟跳着穿过落叶来到近旁——在那片林子里，大多数生灵不识人类，见了人并不怕，反倒比怕他们两人更怕他们的马。这时厄休拉单膝跪着，一手接住拉尔夫，另一只手伸向那只知更鸟；小鸟落在她手腕上，像一只戴着头罩的猎隼似的站在那里，啭起甜美的音符，仿佛在同两位新来者攀谈；厄休拉拿些碎食犒赏它的歌声，它便飞起来停在她肩头，偎着她的脸颊；她幸福地笑了，说：“你瞧，亲爱的，野物不是听懂了我的话，派来这位漂亮的信使，向我们预报一切如意吗？”

“好兆头，”拉尔夫笑道，“可任你亲了又亲，橡树到底还没开口说话呢：瞧，你那知更鸟朋友飞走了——因为你没吃的给它了。”

===Original===

“He is flying towards the Well at the World’s End,” she said, “and biddeth us onward: let us to horse and hasten: for if thou wilt have the whole truth concerning my heart, it is this, that some chance-hap may yet take thee from me ere thou hast drunk of the waters of the Well.”

“Yea,” said Ralph, “and in the innermost of my heart lieth the fear that mayhappen there is no Well, and no healing in it if we find it, and that death, and the backward way may yet sunder us. This is the worst of my heart, and evil is my coward fear.”

But she cast her arms about him and kissed and caressed him, and cried out: “Yea, then fair have been the days of our journeying, and fair this hour of the green oak! And bold and true thine heart that hath led thee thus far, and won thee thy desire of my love.”

So then they armed them, and mounted their horses and set forward. They lived well while they were in the wood, but on the third day they came to where it thinned and at last died out into a stony waste like unto that which they had passed through before they came to the House of the Sorceress, save that this lay in ridges as the waves of a great sea; and these same ridges they were bidden to cross over at their highest, lest they should be bewildered in a maze of little hills and dales leading no whither.

So they entered on this desert, having filled their water-skins at a clear brook, whereat they rejoiced when they found that the face of the wilderness was covered with a salt scurf, and that naught grew there save a sprinkling of small sage bushes.

Now on the second day of their riding this ugly waste, as they came up over the brow of one of these stony ridges, Ralph the farsighted cried out suddenly: “Hold! for I see a man weaponed.”

“Where is he?” quoth Ursula, “and what is he about?” Said Ralph: “He is up yonder on the swell of the next ridge, and by seeming is asleep leaning against a rock.”

Then he bent the Turk bow and set an arrow on the string and they went on warily. When they were down at the foot of the ridge Ralph hailed the man with a lusty cry, but gat no answer of him; so they went on up the bent, till Ralph said: “Now I can see his face under his helm, and it is dark and the eyes are hollow: I will off horse and go up to him afoot, but do thou, beloved, sit still in thy saddle.”

===Chinese===

“它是朝世界尽头之泉飞去的，”她说，“是在催咱们上路呢：上马吧，快些走：因为你要听我心里最实在的话，那就是——只怕在你还没喝上泉水之前，什么意外还会把你从我身边夺走。”

“是啊，”拉尔夫说，“而我心底最深处也埋着恐惧：怕这泉水也许根本不存在，怕找到了也无疗救之效，怕死亡和归途终要把我们分开。这是我心里最黑暗的念头，我这懦弱的恐惧真是可恶。”

她却张开双臂接住他，吻他，抚慰他，喊道：“那又怎样！我们一路走来的日子是那样美好，这绿橡树下的一刻也是这样美好！你的心勇敢而真诚，它引着你走了这么远，也为你赢得了我的爱。”

于是他们披挂整齐，上马前进。在林中的日子过得很舒服，可到第三天，树木渐稀，最后绝迹，化作一片乱石的荒漠，同他们来妖巫之屋之前穿越的那片相仿，只是这片荒漠起伏成垄，像大海的波涛；有人嘱咐过他们，这些石垄要从最高处翻越，免得在那些不通向任何去处的小丘幽谷组成的迷宫里迷失方向。

他们在一条清澈的小溪里灌满了水囊，才踏进这片荒漠；等发现荒原表面结着一层盐霜，除了星星点点的矮小鼠尾草丛外寸草不生时，不禁庆幸先前灌了水。

在这片狰狞荒漠上骑行的第二天，他们正登上一道石垄的坡顶，目光锐利的拉尔夫突然喊道：“站住！我看见一个带兵器的人。”

“他在哪儿？”厄休拉问，“在干什么？”拉尔夫说：“在前头那道石垄的坡脊上，看样子靠着一块岩石睡着了。”

他弯起突厥弓，搭上箭，两人小心翼翼地前进。下到石垄脚下时，拉尔夫放声向那人呼喊，却没有得到回应；他们继续往坡上走，直到拉尔夫说：“现在我看得见他头盔底下的脸了——脸色发黑，眼窝深陷：我下马走过去，你待在马上别动，亲爱的。”

===Original===

But when he had come nigher, he turned and cried out to her: “The man is dead, come anigh.” So she went up to him and dismounted, and they both together stood over the man, who was lying up against a big stone like one at rest. How long he had lain there none knows but God; for in the saltness of the dry desert the flesh had dried on his bones without corrupting, and was as hardened leather. He was in full armour of a strange and ancient fashion, and his sword was girt to his side, neither was there any sign of a wound about him. Under a crag anigh him they found his horse, dead and dry like to himself; and a little way over the brow of the ridge another horse in like case; and close by him a woman whose raiment had not utterly perished, nor her hair; there were gold rings on her arms, and her shoes were done with gold: she had a knife stuck in her breast, with her hand still clutching the handle thereof; so that it seemed that she had herself given herself death.

Ralph and Ursula buried these two with the heaping of stones and went their ways; but some two miles thence they came upon another dead man-at-arms, and near him an old man unweaponed, and they heaped stones on them.

Thereabout night overtook them, and it was dark, so they lay down in the waste, and comforted each other, and slept two or three hours, but arose with the first glimmer of dawn, and mounted and rode forth onward, that they might the sooner be out of that deadly desert, for fear clung to their hearts.

This day, forsooth, they found so many dead folk, that they might not stay to bury them, lest they themselves should come to lie there lacking burial. So they made all the way they might, and rode on some hours by starlight after the night was come, for it was clear and cold. So that at last they were so utterly wearied that they lay down amongst those dead folk, and slept soundly.

===Chinese===

可等他走近些，却转身朝她喊道：“这人死了，过来吧。”她走上前去，下了马，两人一起在那人跟前站定：他靠在一块大石头上，像休息的人一样。他在那里躺了多久，除了上帝无人知晓；因为在这干燥的盐漠里，他肉身枯干在骨头上，并不腐坏，硬得像鞣过的皮革。他穿着一身样式古怪而古老的全副甲胄，佩剑拴在腰间，身上却不见任何伤痕。近旁一块峭壁下，他们找到他的马，同他一样干枯死去；垄顶再过去一点，还有一匹同样死状的马；马身边是一个女子，衣裳和头发都还没有完全朽坏；她臂上戴着金环，鞋上缀着金饰：一把匕首插在她胸口，手还攥着刀柄；看来她是自己结果了自己的性命。

拉尔夫和厄休拉堆石掩埋了这两个人，继续赶路；可约莫两里之外，他们又遇到一具武士的尸骸，近旁还有一个手无寸铁的老人，他们又给这两人堆了石冢。

夜色就在那时追上了他们，天黑了，他们便在荒漠中躺下，彼此安慰着，睡了两三个钟头，天刚透亮就起身，上马前行，只盼早点离开这片致命的荒漠——恐惧攫着他们的心。

这一天，他们见到的死人实在太多，再不能停下来掩埋，唯恐自己也要倒毙在那里无人收殓。于是他们拼命赶路，入夜后又就着星光骑了几个钟头——夜空晴朗而寒冷。到最后他们实在疲惫不堪，便在那些死人中间躺下，沉沉睡去。

===Original===

On the morrow morn Ralph awoke and saw Ursula sleeping peacefully as he deemed, and he looked about on the dreary desert and its dead men and saw no end to it, though they lay on the top of one of those stony bents; and he said softly to himself: “Will it end at all then? Surely all this people of the days gone by were Seekers of the Well as we be; and have they belike turned back from somewhere further on, and might not escape the desert despite of all? Shall we turn now: shall we turn? surely we might get into the kindly wood from here.”

So he spake; but Ursula sat up (for she was not asleep) and said: “The perils of the waste being abundant and exceeding hard to face, would not the Sage or his books have told us of the most deadly?” Said Ralph: “Yet here are all these dead, and we were not told of them, nevertheless we have seen the token on the rocks ofttimes yesterday, so we are yet in the road, unless all this hath been but a snare and a betrayal.”

She shook her head, and was silent a little; then she said: “Ralph, my lad, didst thou see this token (and she set hand to the beads about her neck) on any of those dead folk yesterday?” “Nay,” said Ralph, “though sooth to say I looked for it.” “And I in likewise,” she said; “for indeed I had misgivings as the day grew old; but now I say, let us on in the faith of that token and the kindness of the Sage, and the love of the Innocent People; yea, and thy luck, O lad of the green fields far away, that hath brought thee unscathed so far from Upmeads.”

So they mounted and rode forth, and saw more and more of the dead folk; and ever and anon they looked to them to note if they wore the beads like to them but saw none so dight. Then Ursula said: “Yea, why should the Sage and the books have told us aught of these dead bodies, that are but as the plenishing of the waste; like to the flowers that are cast down before the bier of a saint on a holy-day to be trodden under foot by the churls and the vicars of the close. Forsooth had they been alive now, with swords to smite withal, and hands to drag us into captivity, it had been another matter: but against these I feel bold.”

Ralph sighed, and said: “Yea, but even if we die not in the waste, yet this is piteous; so many lives passed away, so many hopes slain.”

===Chinese===

次日清晨，拉尔夫醒来，看见厄休拉安睡着——他这样以为；他环顾这凄凉的荒漠和满地的死者，虽然他们躺在一道石坡的顶上，却望不见尽头。他轻声自语：“这荒漠到底有没有尽头？这些往昔年代的人，想必都曾是和我们一样的寻泉人吧；他们莫非是从更远的地方折返，终究没能逃出这片荒漠？我们现在回头吗：回头吗？从这里，咱们肯定还能回到那片仁慈的树林里去。”

他这样自言自语；厄休拉却坐了起来（她并没有睡着），说：“这荒漠既然凶险重重、极难穿越，若是有什么最致命的祸患，贤者或者那些书难道会不告诉我们吗？”拉尔夫说：“可这里躺着这么多死人，也没人跟我们提过；不过昨天我们屡屡看见岩石上的记号，所以咱们仍在正路上，除非这一切不过是个圈套、一场背叛。”

她摇摇头，沉默了片刻，然后说：“拉尔夫，我的小伙子，昨天那些死人身上，你可看见过这个记号？”她伸手按着颈间的珠子。“没有，”拉尔夫说，“不过说实话，我找过。”“我也找了，”她说，“天色晚了的时候，我心里确实犯嘀咕；可现在我说，咱们就凭着那记号、凭着贤者的仁爱、凭着无辜之民的深情走下去；对，还有你的运气——你这远方绿野来的小伙子，正是它护着你从阿普米兹平安走过了这么远的路。”

于是他们上马前行，看见的死人越来越多；他们不时凑近察看那些人是否戴着同他们一样的珠子，却一个也没见到。厄休拉说：“可不是嘛，贤者和那些书何必跟我们讲这些尸骸的事呢——它们不过是这荒漠的陈设罢了；就像圣徒的节庆上撒在圣髄前的鲜花，任凭粗汉和教堂的执事踩在脚下。说真的，这些人若是还活着，手里有挥砍的剑、有把我们拖进囚笼的手，那自当别论：对眼前这些，我倒是胆气十足。”

拉尔夫叹道：“话虽如此，就算我们不死在这荒漠里，这也太凄惨了：这么多生命消逝，这么多希望被扼杀。”

===Original===

“Yea,” she said; “but do not folk die there in the world behind us? I have seen sights far worser than this at Utterbol, little while as I was there. Moreover I can note that this army of dead men has not come all in one day or one year, but in a long, long while, by one and two and three; for hast thou not noted that their raiment and war-gear both, is of many fashions, and some much more perished than other, long as things last in this Dry Waste? I say that men die as in the world beyond, but here we see them as they lie dead, and have lain for so long.”

He said: “I fear neither the Waste nor the dead men if thou fearest not, beloved: but I lament for these poor souls.”

“And I also,” said she; “therefore let us on, that we may come to those whose grief we may heal.”

===Chinese===

“是啊，”她说，“可在我们身后的那个世界里，人就不死吗？我在乌特博尔见过比这凄惨得多的光景，尽管我在那里待的时日不长。再说，我看得出，这支死人大军并不是一天一年凑成的，而是悠悠岁月里一个、两个、三个地倒下的；你没注意到吗——他们的衣裳和兵甲式样各异，有的比别的朽坏得多，虽然在这干燥的荒漠里东西经久不烂？我是说，人照旧会死，同外面的世界一样；只不过在这里，我们看见的是他们死去的样子，死了那么久的样子。”

他说：“只要你不怕，亲爱的，我就既不怕这荒漠，也不怕这些死人：我只是哀怜这些可怜的灵魂。”

“我也哀怜，”她说，“所以咱们更该赶路，好去到那些忧愁尚可由我们化解的人身边。”

## XVIII / 十八
===Original===

They Come to the Dry Tree

Presently as they rode they had before them one of the greatest of those land-waves, and they climbed it slowly, going afoot and leading their horses; but when they were but a little way from the brow they saw, over a gap thereof, something, as it were huge horns rising up into the air beyond the crest of the ridge. So they marvelled, and drew their swords, and held them still awhile, misdoubting if this were perchance some terrible monster of the waste; but whereas the thing moved not at all, they plucked up heart and fared on.

So came they to the brow and looked over it into a valley, about which on all sides went the ridge, save where it was broken down into a narrow pass on the further side, so that the said valley was like to one of those theatres of the ancient Roman Folk, whereof are some to be seen in certain lands. Neither did those desert benches lack their sitters; for all down the sides of the valley sat or lay children of men; some women, but most menfolk, of whom the more part were weaponed, and some with their drawn swords in their hands. Whatever semblance of moving was in them was when the eddying wind of the valley stirred the rags of their raiment, or the long hair of the women. But a very midmost of this dreary theatre rose up a huge and monstrous tree, whose topmost branches were even the horns which they had seen from below the hill’s brow. Leafless was that tree and lacking of twigs, and its bole upheld but some fifty of great limbs, and as they looked on it, they doubted whether it were not made by men’s hands rather than grown up out of the earth. All round about the roots of it was a pool of clear water, that cast back the image of the valley-side and the bright sky of the desert, as though it had been a mirror of burnished steel. The limbs of that tree were all behung with blazoned shields and knight’s helms, and swords, and spears, and axes, and hauberks; and it rose up into the air some hundred feet above the flat of the valley.

For a while they looked down silently on to this marvel, then from both their lips at once came the cry **The Dry Tree**. Then Ralph thrust his sword back into his sheath and said: “Meseems I must needs go down amongst them; there is naught to do us harm here; for all these are dead like the others that we saw.”

===Chinese===

他们来到枯树

走着走着，前方又横起一道最大的陆浪，他们下马牵缰，缓缓攀登；离坡顶只差一小段时，他们从山脊的一处豁口望见，脊线之外有一样东西，象是巨大的犄角插进空中。两人心中惊疑，拔出剑，静立了好一会儿，疑心那莫不是荒漠里什么可怕的怪物；但那东西纹丝不动，他们便壮起胆子继续前行。

到了坡顶朝下一望，是一条山谷，四面都围着山脊，只有远端破开一道窄隘口，所以这山谷很象古罗马人的那种圆形剧场——有些地方还能见到那样的遗迹。这片荒漠的看台上也不缺看客：谷坡上上下下，坐着的、躺着的全是人类；有女人，多数是男人，大半带着兵器，有的手里还握着出鞘的剑。他们身上唯一象在动的，是谷中回旋的风吹动他们衣衫的破片，或女人的长发。而在这凄凉剧场的正中央，耸立着一棵巨大怪异的树，树顶的枝桠正是他们从山坡下望见的那对犄角。那树光秃秃的，没有叶子也没有细枝，树干上只撑着五十来根巨枝；他们望着它，竟怀疑这不是地里长出来的，而是人手造出来的。树根四周环绕着一泓清水，映出谷坡和荒漠明亮的天空，就象一面擦亮的钢镜。那树的枝桠上挂满了绘有纹章的盾、骑士盔、剑、矛、斧和锁子甲；树身高高伸入空中，离谷底足有百来尺。

他们默默俯视这奇景好一会儿，随后两人同时脱口迸出一声呼喊：**枯树**！拉尔夫把剑插回鞘中，说：「看来我非下去到他们中间走一遭不可；这里没有什么会伤害我们；因为这些人同我们先前见过的一样，都是死的。」

===Original===

Ursula turned to him with burning cheeks and sparkling eyes, and said eagerly: “Yea, yea, let us go down, else might we chance to miss something that we ought to wot of.”

Therewith she also sheathed her sword, and they went both of them down together, and that easily; for as aforesaid the slope was as if it had been cut into steps for their feet. And as they passed by the dead folk, for whom they had often to turn aside, they noted that each of the dead leathery faces was drawn up in a grin as though they had died in pain, and yet beguiled, so that all those visages looked somewhat alike, as though they had come from the workshop of one craftsman.

At last Ralph and Ursula stood on the level ground underneath the Tree, and they looked up at the branches, and down to the water at their feet; and now it seemed to them as though the Tree had verily growth in it, for they beheld its roots, that they went out from the mound or islet of earth into the water, and spread abroad therein, and seemed to waver about.
